summary: Resolved IWC-REQ-171's architectural ownership question for Publication Handoff execution (architecture only, no implementation). Bootstrapped a governed session, then independently read in full: docs/contracts/INTERACTIVE_WORKFLOW_CONTRACT.md (IWC-001 v1.1), docs/contracts/CANONICAL_HUMAN_GOVERNANCE_RECORD_CONTRACT.md (CHGR-001), docs/contracts/TYPED_AUTHORITY_MODEL_CONSUMPTION_CONTRACT.md (TAMC-001), docs/contracts/TYPED_AUTHORITY_MODEL_PRODUCTION_CONSUMPTION_CONTRACT.md (TAMPC-001), the Canonical Phase Finalization Architecture (Phase 134), the Canonical Lifecycle State Authority Architecture (Phase 135) and Governance Lifecycle Pattern Architecture (Phase 137V), the Track 135/136 publication-schema and rehearsal documents, phase reports 143J and 143K-143P, and PROJECT_STATUS.md, cross-checked against source (src/pcae/interactive_workflow/**, src/pcae/commands/governance_record.py, src/pcae/lifecycle.py). Evaluated four candidate architectures for Publication Handoff execution ownership. Option A (Interactive Workflow owns publication) rejected: contradicts IWC-001 Sec1's frozen rule that a Decision Session is never itself published. Option B (Lifecycle Finalization owns publication) rejected: no PCAE phase/task lifecycle component has any established relationship to CHGR; both contracts independently classify that domain as unrelated. Option C (a dedicated Publication Coordinator) selected: a new, minimal component external to interactive_workflow whose sole input is the already-frozen PublicationReadinessPackage and whose sole output is CHGR-001 Sec8's atomic write, satisfying one-owner-per-responsibility, authority neutrality, fail-closed behavior, determinism, and immutable-evidence requirements without reopening any frozen contract section. Three Option D sub-variants (CLI-inline write, Confirmation-performs-write, distributed per-component writes) evaluated and rejected. Central non-obvious finding: reaching Confirmed and package readiness are necessary but not sufficient to publish -- CHGR-001 Sec17's no-self-authorization rule excludes any autonomous publish-when-ready trigger outright, so an explicit, human-operated publication-authorization event, distinct from Confirmation, is architecturally required. Delivered ownership rationale, alternative analysis, dependency analysis, lifecycle interaction model, authority boundary analysis, risk analysis, a four-phase implementation roadmap (144B Contract Freeze / 144C Implementation / 144D Independent Verification, none authorized by this phase), and a full requirement traceability matrix. Zero files under src/, tests/, or docs/contracts/** were created or modified. See docs/PHASE_144A_PUBLICATION_EXECUTION_OWNERSHIP_ARCHITECTURE.md.
